claim: Mutations that activate LRRK2 protein kinase cause Parkinson's disease.
source: Mutations that activate LRRK2 protein kinase cause Parkinson's disease.
evidence: This is a well-established fact in the field, supported by citations in the introduction.

claim: LRRK2 phosphorylates a subset of Rab GTPases within their Switch-II motif controlling interaction with effectors.
source: LRRK2 phosphorylates a subset of Rab GTPases within their Switch-II motif controlling interaction with effectors.
evidence: This is stated in the abstract and supported by citations to previous work (Steger et al., 2016; Steger et al., 2017).

claim: An siRNA screen of all human protein phosphatases revealed that PPM1H counteracts LRRK2 signaling by specifically dephosphorylating Rab proteins.
source: An siRNA screen of all human protein phosphatases revealed that a poorly studied protein phosphatase, PPM1H, counteracts LRRK2 signaling by specifically dephosphorylating Rab proteins.
evidence: This is a primary finding of the study, supported by the siRNA screen data presented in Figure 2.

claim: PPM1H knockout increased endogenous Rab phosphorylation in human A549 cells.
source: PPM1H knockout increased endogenous Rab phosphorylation and inhibited Rab dephosphorylation in human A549 cells.
evidence: This is supported by data in Figure 6A showing increased Rab10 phosphorylation in PPM1H knockout cells.

claim: PPM1H knockout inhibited Rab dephosphorylation in human A549 cells.
source: PPM1H knockout increased endogenous Rab phosphorylation and inhibited Rab dephosphorylation in human A549 cells.
evidence: This is supported by data in Figure 7 showing delayed dephosphorylation of Rab10 following LRRK2 inhibitor treatment in PPM1H knockout cells.

claim: Overexpression of PPM1H suppressed LRRK2-mediated Rab phosphorylation.
source: Overexpression of PPM1H suppressed LRRK2-mediated Rab phosphorylation.
evidence: This is supported by data in Figures 3B, 3C, and 4 showing reduced Rab phosphorylation when PPM1H is overexpressed.

claim: PPM1H efficiently and directly dephosphorylated Rab8A in biochemical studies.
source: PPM1H also efficiently and directly dephosphorylated Rab8A in biochemical studies.
evidence: This is supported by in vitro phosphatase assay data in Figure 8.

claim: A substrate-trapping PPM1H mutant (Asp288Ala) binds with high affinity to endogenous, LRRK2-phosphorylated Rab proteins.
source: A "substrate-trapping" PPM1H mutant (Asp288Ala) binds with high affinity to endogenous, LRRK2-phosphorylated Rab proteins, thereby blocking dephosphorylation seen upon addition of LRRK2 inhibitors.
evidence: This is supported by co-immunoprecipitation data in Figure 9A and mass spectrometry data in Figure 9B.

claim: PPM1H[D288A] blocks dephosphorylation of Rab proteins seen upon addition of LRRK2 inhibitors.
source: A "substrate-trapping" PPM1H mutant (Asp288Ala) binds with high affinity to endogenous, LRRK2-phosphorylated Rab proteins, thereby blocking dephosphorylation seen upon addition of LRRK2 inhibitors.
evidence: This is supported by data in Figure 9—figure supplement 1C and Figure 9—figure supplement 2C showing delayed dephosphorylation in cells expressing PPM1H[D288A].

claim: PPM1H is localized to the Golgi.
source: PPM1H is localized to the Golgi and its knockdown suppresses primary cilia formation, similar to pathogenic LRRK2.
evidence: This is supported by immunofluorescence microscopy data in Figure 10 showing co-localization of PPM1H with Golgi markers.

claim: PPM1H knockdown suppresses primary cilia formation.
source: PPM1H is localized to the Golgi and its knockdown suppresses primary cilia formation, similar to pathogenic LRRK2.
evidence: This is supported by data in Figure 11 showing reduced ciliation in MEF cells with PPM1H knockdown.

claim: PPM1H acts as a key modulator of LRRK2 signaling by controlling dephosphorylation of Rab proteins.
source: Thus, PPM1H acts as a key modulator of LRRK2 signaling by controlling dephosphorylation of Rab proteins.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the collective data presented in the study.

claim: PPM1H activity enhancers could offer a new therapeutic approach to prevent or treat Parkinson's disease.
source: PPM1H activity enhancers could offer a new therapeutic approach to prevent or treat Parkinson's disease.
evidence: This is a speculative statement based on the findings of the study.

claim: Missense mutations within the GTPase domain (N1437H, R1441G/C, Y1699C) and kinase domains (G2019S, I2020T) hyper-activate LRRK2 protein kinase and cause Parkinson's disease (PD) (Zimprich et al., 2004; Paisán-Ruíz et al., 2004; Alessi and Sammler, 2018).
source: Missense mutations within the GTPase domain (N1437H, R1441G/C, Y1699C) and kinase domains (G2019S, I2020T) hyper-activate LRRK2 protein kinase and cause Parkinson's disease (PD) (Zimprich et al., 2004; Paisán-Ruíz et al., 2004; Alessi and Sammler, 2018).
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous studies.

claim: Mutations in LRRK2 are one of the most common genetic causes of familial Parkinson's comprising ~5% of familial Parkinson's, and ~1% of sporadic Parkinson's patients (Healy et al., 2008; Domingo and Klein, 2018).
source: Mutations in LRRK2 are one of the most common genetic causes of familial Parkinson's comprising ~5% of familial Parkinson's, and ~1% of sporadic Parkinson's patients (Healy et al., 2008; Domingo and Klein, 2018).
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous studies.

claim: LRRK2 mediated Parkinson's closely resembles the common sporadic form of the disease affecting the vast majority of patients (Marras et al., 2011).
source: In terms of clinical presentation and late age of onset, LRRK2 mediated Parkinson's closely resembles the common sporadic form of the disease affecting the vast majority of patients (Marras et al., 2011).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to a previous study.

claim: The G2019S mutation, located within the magnesium binding motif of the kinase domain, is the most common LRRK2 mutation and activates LRRK2 kinase activity around 2-fold (West et al., 2005; Greggio et al., 2006; Jaleel et al., 2007).
source: The G2019S mutation, located within the magnesium binding motif of the kinase domain, is the most common LRRK2 mutation and activates LRRK2 kinase activity around 2-fold (West et al., 2005; Greggio et al., 2006; Jaleel et al., 2007).
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous studies.

claim: Penetrance of the G2019S and other pathogenic LRRK2 mutations is incomplete (Ruiz-Martínez et al., 2010; Goldwurm et al., 2011).
source: Penetrance of the G2019S and other pathogenic LRRK2 mutations is incomplete (Ruiz-Martínez et al., 2010; Goldwurm et al., 2011).
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous studies.

claim: There is emerging evidence that the LRRK2 pathway is hyperactivated in some patients with idiopathic PD (Di Maio et al., 2018).
source: There is emerging evidence that the LRRK2 pathway is hyperactivated in some patients with idiopathic PD (Di Maio et al., 2018).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to a previous study.

claim: LRRK2 phosphorylates a subgroup of Rab proteins (Rab3A/B/C/D, Rab8A/B, Rab10, Rab12, Rab29, Rab35, and Rab43) at a conserved Thr/Ser residue (Thr73 for Rab10), located at the center of the effector binding switch-II motif (Steger et al., 2016; Steger et al., 2017; Jeong et al., 2018).
source: Recent studies have revealed that LRRK2 phosphorylates a subgroup of Rab proteins (Rab3A/B/C/D, Rab8A/B, Rab10, Rab12, Rab29, Rab35, and Rab43) at a conserved Thr/Ser residue (Thr73 for Rab10), located at the center of the effector binding switch-II motif (Steger et al., 2016; Steger et al., 2017; Jeong et al., 2018).
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous studies.

claim: All established pathogenic mutations enhance LRRK2 mediated Rab protein phosphorylation in a manner that is blocked by diverse LRRK2 inhibitors (Steger et al., 2016; Steger et al., 2017; Ito et al., 2016).
source: Consistent with Rab proteins comprising disease-relevant substrates, all established pathogenic mutations enhance LRRK2 mediated Rab protein phosphorylation in a manner that is blocked by diverse LRRK2 inhibitors (Steger et al., 2016; Steger et al., 2017; Ito et al., 2016).
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous studies.

claim: LRRK2 phosphorylation of Rab proteins blocks the ability of Rab proteins to interact with cognate effectors such as GDI and guanine nucleotide exchange factors, thereby trapping the phosphorylated Rab protein in the GTP bound state on the membrane where it has been phosphorylated (Steger et al., 2016; Pfeffer, 2018).
source: LRRK2 phosphorylation of Rab proteins blocks the ability of Rab proteins to interact with cognate effectors such as GDI and guanine nucleotide exchange factors, thereby trapping the phosphorylated Rab protein in the GTP bound state on the membrane where it has been phosphorylated (Steger et al., 2016; Pfeffer, 2018).
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous studies.

claim: A novel group of effectors including RILPL1 and RILPL2 bind preferentially to LRRK2 phosphorylated Rab8 and Rab10 (Steger et al., 2017).
source: Recent work identified a novel group of effectors including RILPL1 and RILPL2 that bind preferentially to LRRK2 phosphorylated Rab8 and Rab10 (Steger et al., 2017).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to a previous study.

claim: LRRK2 phosphorylated Rab8A and Rab10, in complex with RILPL1/RILPL2, inhibit the formation of primary cilia that are implicated in controlling a Sonic hedgehog-driven neuroprotective pathway that could provide a mechanism by which LRRK2 is linked to PD (Dhekne et al., 2018).
source: LRRK2 phosphorylated Rab8A and Rab10, in complex with RILPL1/RILPL2, inhibit the formation of primary cilia that are implicated in controlling a Sonic hedgehog-driven neuroprotective pathway that could provide a mechanism by which LRRK2 is linked to PD (Dhekne et al., 2018).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to a previous study.

claim: Rab29 (Purlyte et al., 2018; Liu et al., 2018) and VPS35 (Mir et al., 2018) regulate phosphorylation of Rab proteins via LRRK2.
source: Other research has revealed that components implicated in PD including Rab29 (Purlyte et al., 2018; Liu et al., 2018) and VPS35 (Mir et al., 2018) also regulate phosphorylation of Rab proteins via LRRK2.
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous studies.

claim: Treatment of cell lines with LRRK2 inhibitors induce rapid dephosphorylation of Rab10 within 1-2 min (Ito et al., 2016).
source: The protein phosphatase(s) that act on LRRK2 phosphorylated Rab proteins have not been identified, but appear to be highly active, as treatment of cell lines with LRRK2 inhibitors induce rapid dephosphorylation of Rab10 within 1-2 min (Ito et al., 2016).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to a previous study.

claim: Dephosphorylation of LRRK2 at Ser935 occurs much more slowly in response to LRRK2 inhibitor administration, requiring up to 90 min (Ito et al., 2016).
source: In contrast, dephosphorylation of LRRK2 at a well-studied potential autophosphorylation site (Ser935) occurs much more slowly in response to LRRK2 inhibitor administration, requiring up to 90 min (Ito et al., 2016).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to a previous study.

claim: Only a small proportion (around 1%) of the total cellular Rab proteins are phosphorylated (Steger et al., 2016; Ito et al., 2016).
source: Only a small proportion (around 1%) of the total cellular Rab proteins are phosphorylated (Steger et al., 2016; Ito et al., 2016).
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous studies.

claim: PP1 or PP2A phosphatases do not dephosphorylate Rab proteins.
source: PP1 or PP2A phosphatases do not dephosphorylate Rab proteins
evidence: This is supported by data in Figure 1 showing that calyculin-A and okadaic acid did not significantly impact Rab10 or Rab12 dephosphorylation following LRRK2 inhibitor treatment.

claim: Calyculin-A (PP1 inhibitor) and okadaic acid (PP2A inhibitor) did not have a significant impact on basal phosphorylation of Rab10 (Thr73) or Rab12 (Ser105) or dephosphorylation following administration of MLi-2.
source: Wild-type and LRRK2[R1441C] knock-in mouse embryonic fibroblasts (MEF cells) were treated with 0.1 µM calyculin-A (PP1 inhibitor) or 1 µM Okadaic acid (PP2A inhibitor) (Ishihara et al., 1989), and neither of these agents had a significant impact on basal phosphorylation of Rab10 (Thr73) or Rab12 (Ser105) or dephosphorylation following administration of the well-characterized highly selective and potent LRRK2 inhibitor termed MLi-2 (Fell et al., 2015) (Figure 1).
evidence: This is supported by data in Figure 1.

claim: PP1 phosphatase regulates dephosphorylation of LRRK2 at Ser935 (Lobbestael et al., 2013).
source: Consistent with PP1 phosphatase regulating dephosphorylation of LRRK2 at Ser935 (Lobbestael et al., 2013), calyculin-A stimulated Ser935 phosphorylation, particularly in the LRRK2[R1441C] MEF cells.
evidence: This is supported by a citation to a previous study and data in Figure 1.

claim: Calyculin-A stimulated Ser935 phosphorylation, particularly in the LRRK2[R1441C] MEF cells.
source: Consistent with PP1 phosphatase regulating dephosphorylation of LRRK2 at Ser935 (Lobbestael et al., 2013), calyculin-A stimulated Ser935 phosphorylation, particularly in the LRRK2[R1441C] MEF cells.
evidence: This is supported by data in Figure 1.

claim: Calyculin-A prevented dephosphorylation of Ser935 following administration of MLi-2.
source: It also prevented dephosphorylation of Ser935 following administration of MLi-2 (Figure 1).
evidence: This is supported by data in Figure 1.

claim: At 1 µM, Okadaic acid is likely to partially inhibit PP1 (Ishihara et al., 1989).
source: At 1 µM, Okadaic acid is likely to partially inhibit PP1 (Ishihara et al., 1989); this concentration also blocked MLi-2 from inducing dephosphorylation of Ser935.
evidence: This is supported by a citation to a previous study.

claim: 1 µM okadaic acid blocked MLi-2 from inducing dephosphorylation of Ser935.
source: At 1 µM, Okadaic acid is likely to partially inhibit PP1 (Ishihara et al., 1989); this concentration also blocked MLi-2 from inducing dephosphorylation of Ser935.
evidence: This is supported by data in Figure 1.

claim: Calyculin-A, but not okadaic acid promoted phosphorylation of the PP1 substrate MYPT1 (Thr853) (Dimopoulos et al., 2007; Hutchinson et al., 2011; Westphal et al., 1999).
source: Calyculin-A, but not okadaic acid promoted phosphorylation of the PP1 substrate MYPT1 (Thr853) (Dimopoulos et al., 2007; Hutchinson et al., 2011; Westphal et al., 1999).
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous studies and data in Figure 1.

claim: Calyculin-A and okadaic acid activated the S6K1 kinase pathway as judged by increase in S6K1 phosphorylation (Thr389, mTORC1 site) that is regulated by PP1 and PP2A.
source: Calyculin-A and okadaic acid also activated the S6K1 kinase pathway as judged by increase in S6K1 phosphorylation (Thr389, mTORC1 site) that is regulated by PP1 and PP2A (Figure 1).
evidence: This is supported by data in Figure 1.

claim: A library consisting of 322 siRNAs (Dharmacon) targeting 264 phosphatase catalytic subunits (189 protein phosphatases, 26 halo acid dehalogenase phosphatases, 18 chloroperoxidases, 5 nucleoside-diphosphate-linked moiety-X phosphatases and 7 carbohydrate phosphatases) as well as 56 characterized regulatory subunits was assembled.
source: We assembled a library consisting of 322 siRNAs (Dharmacon) targeting 264 phosphatase catalytic subunits (189 protein phosphatases, 26 halo acid dehalogenase phosphatases, 18 chloroperoxidases, 5 nucleoside-diphosphate-linked moiety-X phosphatases and 7 carbohydrate phosphatases) as well as 56 characterized regulatory subunits (Supplementary file 1).
evidence: This is a description of the experimental design.

claim: Two replicate screens were undertaken in which cells were treated with siRNA targeting each phosphatase component for 72 h before cell lysis (Screen 1 and 2).
source: Two replicate screens were undertaken in which cells were treated with siRNA targeting each phosphatase component for 72 h before cell lysis (Screen 1 and 2, Figure 2A and B).
evidence: This is a description of the experimental design.

claim: A third screen was performed in which partial dephosphorylation of Rab10 was induced by adding MLi-2 inhibitor for 5 min prior to cell lysis (Screen 3).
source: A third screen was also performed in which partial dephosphorylation of Rab10 was induced by adding MLi-2 inhibitor for 5 min prior to cell lysis (Screen 3, Figure 2A and C).
evidence: This is a description of the experimental design.

claim: The top hits that enhanced Rab10 protein phosphorylation over 1.5-fold in Screen 1 and 2 were PPM1H, TAB1, PTPN6, PTPN22, PTPN23, MTMR9 and NT5DC2.
source: The top hits that enhanced Rab10 protein phosphorylation over 1.5-fold in Screen 1 and 2 were PPM1H (Metal-dependent protein phosphatases [PPM] family serine/threonine phosphatase), TAB1 (PPM family catalytically inactive pseudophosphatase), PTPN6 (tyrosine phosphatase) PTPN22 (tyrosine phosphatase), PTPN23 (tyrosine phosphatase), MTMR9 (myotubularin lipid phosphatase) and NT5DC2 (nucleoside-diphosphate-linked moiety-X phosphatase) (Figure 2B).
evidence: This is supported by data in Figure 2B.

claim: In screen 3 the top hits were PPM1H, DUSP3, DUSP18 and PLPP6.
source: In screen 3 the top hits were PPM1H, DUSP3 (dual specificity phosphatase), DUSP18 (dual specificity phosphatase) and PLPP6 (presqualene diphosphate phosphatase) (Figure 2C).
evidence: This is supported by data in Figure 2C.

claim: 5 phosphatases (GAK, ALPI, PPEF2, MDP1, PUDP) when knocked-down, significantly reduced Rab10 phosphorylation.
source: We also identified 5 phosphatases (GAK, ALPI, PPEF2, MDP1, PUDP) that when knocked-down, significantly reduced Rab10 phosphorylation (Figure 2B).
evidence: This is supported by data in Figure 2B.

claim: PPM1H was observed as a significant hit in all 3 screens.
source: PPM1H was observed as a significant hit in all 3 screens.
evidence: This is supported by data in Figures 2B and 2C.

claim: PPM1H was the top serine/threonine phosphatase in each of the screens.
source: It was also the top serine/threonine phosphatase in each of the screens.
evidence: This is supported by data in Figures 2B and 2C.

claim: Human PPM1H possesses 514 residues encompassing a PPM type phosphatase domain with no other known functional motifs (Chen et al., 2017).
source: Human PPM1H possesses 514 residues encompassing a PPM type phosphatase domain with no other known functional motifs (Chen et al., 2017).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to a previous study.

claim: siRNA mediated depletion of PPM1H increased Rab10 phosphorylation, without affecting overall levels of Rab10 or LRRK2.
source: Repeat studies in multiple experiments confirmed that siRNA mediated depletion of PPM1H increased Rab10 phosphorylation, without affecting overall levels of Rab10 or LRRK2 (Figures 2D, E and 3A).
evidence: This is supported by data in Figures 2D, 2E, and 3A.

claim: Endogenous PPM1H, detected by immunoblot, migrates as a doublet of ~55 kDa.
source: Consistent with previous work (Lee-Hoeflich et al., 2011), we observed that endogenous PPM1H, detected by immunoblot, migrates as a doublet of ~55 kDa (reason for doublet unknown) with the top band migrating at the expected molecular weight for full length PPM1H.
evidence: This is supported by a citation to a previous study and data in Figure 3A.

claim: Expression of both forms of PPM1H was lowered by siRNA treatment.
source: Expression of both forms of PPM1H was lowered by siRNA treatment.
evidence: This is supported by data in Figure 3A.

claim: siRNA knockdown of NT5DC2 enhanced Rab10 phosphorylation without impacting total Rab10 or LRRK2 levels, or LRRK2 Ser935 phosphorylation.
source: We also confirmed that siRNA knockdown of NT5DC2 (Figure 2D), DUSP3, DUSP18 and PLPP6 (Figure 2E) enhanced Rab10 phosphorylation without impacting total Rab10 or LRRK2 levels, or LRRK2 Ser935 phosphorylation.
evidence: This is supported by data in Figures 2D and 2E.

claim: siRNA knockdown of DUSP3 enhanced Rab10 phosphorylation without impacting total Rab10 or LRRK2 levels, or LRRK2 Ser935 phosphorylation.
source: We also confirmed that siRNA knockdown of NT5DC2 (Figure 2D), DUSP3, DUSP18 and PLPP6 (Figure 2E) enhanced Rab10 phosphorylation without impacting total Rab10 or LRRK2 levels, or LRRK2 Ser935 phosphorylation.
evidence: This is supported by data in Figure 2E.

claim: siRNA knockdown of DUSP18 enhanced Rab10 phosphorylation without impacting total Rab10 or LRRK2 levels, or LRRK2 Ser935 phosphorylation.
source: We also confirmed that siRNA knockdown of NT5DC2 (Figure 2D), DUSP3, DUSP18 and PLPP6 (Figure 2E) enhanced Rab10 phosphorylation without impacting total Rab10 or LRRK2 levels, or LRRK2 Ser935 phosphorylation.
evidence: This is supported by data in Figure 2E.

claim: siRNA knockdown of PLPP6 enhanced Rab10 phosphorylation without impacting total Rab10 or LRRK2 levels, or LRRK2 Ser935 phosphorylation.
source: We also confirmed that siRNA knockdown of NT5DC2 (Figure 2D), DUSP3, DUSP18 and PLPP6 (Figure 2E) enhanced Rab10 phosphorylation without impacting total Rab10 or LRRK2 levels, or LRRK2 Ser935 phosphorylation.
evidence: This is supported by data in Figure 2E.

claim: Knock-down of the tyrosine phosphatases PTPN6, PTPN22, PTPN23 and the possible inositol phosphatase MTMR9 significantly reduced Rab10 protein levels (without affecting total LRRK2) and therefore potentially increase the calculated phospho-Rab10/total Rab10 ratio.
source: However, knock-down of the tyrosine phosphatases PTPN6, PTPN22, PTPN23 and the possible inositol phosphatase MTMR9 significantly reduced Rab10 protein levels (without affecting total LRRK2) and therefore potentially increase the calculated phospho-Rab10/total Rab10 ratio (Figure 2D).
evidence: This is supported by data in Figure 2D.

claim: siRNA depletion of TAB1 enhanced Rab10 protein phosphorylation to a marginal extent in repeat experiments.
source: siRNA depletion of TAB1 enhanced Rab10 protein phosphorylation to a marginal extent in repeat experiments (Figure 2D).
evidence: This is supported by data in Figure 2D.

claim: Knock-down of GAK, ALPI, PPEF2, MDP1, and PUDP markedly decreased LRRK2 expression, likely accounting for the decreases in Rab10 phosphorylation observed.
source: Knock-down of GAK, ALPI, PPEF2, MDP1, and PUDP markedly decreased LRRK2 expression, likely accounting for the decreases in Rab10 phosphorylation observed (Figure 2F).
evidence: This is supported by data in Figure 2F.

claim: Overexpression of wild-type PPM1H strikingly ablated the phosphorylation of Rab10 observed following overexpression of the LRRK2[R1441G] pathogenic mutant.
source: Overexpression of wild-type, PPM1H strikingly ablated the phosphorylation of Rab10 observed following overexpression of the LRRK2[R1441G] pathogenic mutant (Figure 3B).
evidence: This is supported by data in Figure 3B.

claim: Mutation of His153 to Leu markedly reduced PPM1H protein expression.
source: We found that mutation of His153 to residues such as Leu that was used in a previous study (Lee-Hoeflich et al., 2011), markedly reduced protein expression, whereas mutation of this residue to Asp preserved similar expression to wild-type levels.
evidence: This is a description of experimental observations.

claim: Mutation of His153 to Asp preserved similar expression to wild-type levels.
source: We found that mutation of His153 to residues such as Leu that was used in a previous study (Lee-Hoeflich et al., 2011), markedly reduced protein expression, whereas mutation of this residue to Asp preserved similar expression to wild-type levels.
evidence: This is a description of experimental observations.

claim: Overexpression of PPM1H[H153D] catalytic mutant failed to induce dephosphorylation of Rab10.
source: Overexpression of PPM1H[H153D] catalytic mutant failed to induce dephosphorylation of Rab10 (Figure 3B)
evidence: This is supported by data in Figure 3B.

claim: Overexpression of wild-type, but not catalytically inactive PPM1H blocked phosphorylation of Rab8A.
source: Similarly, overexpression of wild-type, but not catalytically inactive PPM1H blocked phosphorylation of Rab8A (Figure 3C) as well as Rab3A, Rab3B, Rab3C, Rab3D, Rab8B, Rab12, Rab35 and Rab43 (Figure 3—figure supplement 1A–1H).
evidence: This is supported by data in Figure 3C and Figure 3—figure supplement 1.

claim: Overexpression of wild-type, but not catalytically inactive PPM1H blocked phosphorylation of Rab3A, Rab3B, Rab3C, Rab3D, Rab8B, Rab12, Rab35 and Rab43.
source: Similarly, overexpression of wild-type, but not catalytically inactive PPM1H blocked phosphorylation of Rab8A (Figure 3C) as well as Rab3A, Rab3B, Rab3C, Rab3D, Rab8B, Rab12, Rab35 and Rab43 (Figure 3—figure supplement 1A–1H).
evidence: This is supported by data in Figure 3—figure supplement 1.

claim: Overexpression of PPM1H did not suppress phosphorylation of Rab8A at the Ser111 site induced following activation of the PINK1 kinase by addition of the mitochondrial uncoupler, CCCP (Lai et al., 2015).
source: In contrast, overexpression of PPM1H did not suppress phosphorylation of Rab8A at the Ser111 site induced following activation of the PINK1 kinase by addition of the mitochondrial uncoupler, CCCP (Lai et al., 2015) (Figure 3—figure supplement 2A).
evidence: This is supported by data in Figure 3—figure supplement 2A.

claim: Overexpression of PPM1H did not impact the phosphorylation of key markers of the Akt and AMPK signaling pathways.
source: In addition, overexpression of PPM1H did not impact the phosphorylation of key markers of the Akt and AMPK signaling pathways (Figure 3—figure supplement 2B).
evidence: This is supported by data in Figure 3—figure supplement 2B.

claim: In cells not expressing either PPM1H form, phosphorylated Rab10 (detected using a phosphoRab10-specific antibody) was concentrated over peri-centriolar membranes, with a narrower localization than total Rab10 in these cells (Dhekne et al., 2018).
source: As observed previously, in cells not expressing either PPM1H form, phosphorylated Rab10 (detected using a phosphoRab10-specific antibody) was concentrated over peri-centriolar membranes, with a narrower localization than total Rab10 in these cells (Dhekne et al., 2018).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to a previous study and data in Figure 4.

claim: In cells expressing wild-type PPM1H (but not its catalytically inactive forms), levels of phosphorylated Rab10 were markedly reduced if not abolished.
source: However, in cells expressing wild-type PPM1H (but not its catalytically inactive forms), levels of phosphorylated Rab10 were markedly reduced if not abolished (Figure 4).
evidence: This is supported by data in Figure 4.

claim: PPM1M suppressed Rab10 and Rab8A phosphorylation in cells, albeit to a lower extent than PPM1H.
source: We found that PPM1M but not PPM1J suppressed Rab10 and Rab8A phosphorylation in cells, albeit to a lower extent than PPM1H (Figure 5A).
evidence: This is supported by data in Figure 5A.

claim: PPM1J did not suppress Rab10 and Rab8A phosphorylation in cells.
source: We found that PPM1M but not PPM1J suppressed Rab10 and Rab8A phosphorylation in cells, albeit to a lower extent than PPM1H (Figure 5A).
evidence: This is supported by data in Figure 5A.

claim: There are 20 PPM family phosphatases in humans.
source: There are 20 PPM family phosphatases in humans (Figure 5B).
evidence: This is supported by a phylogenetic tree in Figure 5B.

claim: Only PHLPP1 (Brognard et al., 2007) moderately reduced Rab10 phosphorylation out of 10 other PPM members tested (TAB1, PPM1K, PPM1D, PPM1E, PPM1F, ILKAP, PPM1G, PPM1B, PPM1A, PHLPP1).
source: In addition to PPM1M and PPM1J, we probed 10 other PPM members (TAB1, PPM1K, PPM1D, PPM1E, PPM1F, ILKAP, PPM1G, PPM1B, PPM1A, PHLPP1) and found that only PHLPP1 (Brognard et al., 2007) moderately reduced Rab10 phosphorylation (Figure 5C).
evidence: This is supported by data in Figure 5C.

claim: CRISPR-Cas9 guides were designed to target exon-1 of the PPM1H gene and would be predicted to ablate expression of the full length PPM1H protein but may not impact expression of a shorter splice variant that lacks exon-1.
source: CRISPR-Cas9 guides were designed to target exon-1 of the PPM1H gene and would be predicted to ablate expression of the full length PPM1H protein but may not impact expression of a shorter splice variant that lacks exon-1.
evidence: This is a description of the experimental design.

claim: 5 independent clones demonstrated complete loss of the full length PPM1H protein by immunoblot analysis.
source: We isolated 5 independent clones that demonstrated complete loss of the full length PPM1H protein by immunoblot analysis.
evidence: This is supported by data in Figure 6A.

claim: These clones still possessed the lower species detected with the PPM1H antibody and indeed, expression of this form appeared to be upregulated in two of the cell lines.
source: These clones still possessed the lower species detected with the PPM1H antibody and indeed, expression of this form appeared to be upregulated in two of the cell lines (Figure 6A).
evidence: This is supported by data in Figure 6A.

claim: A complete PPM1H knock-out cell line in which both the upper and lower species of PPM1H were knocked-out was generated using CRISPR-Cas9 guides targeting exon 4 of PPM1H.
source: We also generated a complete PPM1H knock-out cell line in which both the upper and lower species of PPM1H were knocked-out, using CRISPR-Cas9 guides targeting exon 4 of PPM1H.
evidence: This is a description of the experimental design.

claim: Basal levels of Rab10 phosphorylation was increased 2-5-fold in 10 independent knock-out cell lines compared to 4 wild-type cell clones.
source: Basal levels of Rab10 phosphorylation was increased 2-5-fold in 10 independent knock-out cell lines that we examined compared to 4 wild-type cell clones that had been through all of the equivalent steps including clonal selection (Figure 6A).
evidence: This is supported by data in Figure 6A.

claim: The stoichiometry of Rab protein phosphorylation in wild-type A549 cells was ~0.8%.
source: This revealed that the stoichiometry of Rab protein phosphorylation in wild-type A549 cells was ~0.8% (Figure 6B), similar to values obtained in previous work in different cell types using mass spectrometry (Steger et al., 2016) or Phos-tag analysis (Ito et al., 2016).
evidence: This is supported by data in Figure 6B.

claim: In the PPM1H knock-out cells the stoichiometry of Rab protein phosphorylation increased to ~2.6%.
source: In the PPM1H knock-out cells the stoichiometry of Rab protein phosphorylation increased to ~2.6% (Figure 6B).
evidence: This is supported by data in Figure 6B.

claim: In addition to Rab10, phosphorylated forms of Rab8A and Rab35 were enriched in the PPM1H knock-out cell lines in comparison to wild-type.
